tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the project's purpose as a host-neutral orchestration workspace for reusable AI Powers, multiple product systems, local model providers, and agent hosts.

tour.title: Agent Routing Bible
tour.description: Read AGENTS.md to understand the central routing instructions that define Power roles, host neutrality rules, provider configuration, and gate event behavior for all agents.

tour.title: CLI Entrypoints
tour.description: Explore how the dw CLI is launched across platforms. bin/dw is the Bash entrypoint that delegates to Python scripts based on subcommand.

tour.title: Power Runtime v2
tour.description: Dive into the Python CLI modules that implement workspace, power, host, provider, and system commands. dw_cli.py is the main runtime (~935 lines), dw_entry.py handles one-click bootstrap commands.

tour.title: Power Manifests
tour.description: Examine the Power manifests that declare capabilities, distribution modes, host support, and permissions for each registered Power (gwc, ua, task-me, bmad).

tour.title: Host Adapters
tour.description: See how each AI host gets thin generated adapters that contain only routing instructions. The adapters in .kilo/, .github/, .agents/, .claude/, .codex/, .kiro/, and .clinerules/ all point to the same canonical Power logic.

tour.title: Powers
tour.description: Tour the reusable AI capability modules. powers/gwc provides governance, powers/ua provides semantic analysis, powers/task-me provides implementation planning, and powers/bmad is the release-first BMAD Method router.

tour.title: Distribution System
tour.description: Understand how Powers are packaged and distributed. power_dist.py builds deterministic ZIPs with SHA-256 manifests. schemas/ defines JSON contracts. templates/ provides portable runtime templates injected into every distributed package.

tour.title: BMAD Plugin
tour.description: Explore the BMAD Method Power plugin, which overlays DW-specific files (bootstrap scripts, configs, contracts) onto the upstream BMAD-METHOD repository without forking it.

tour.title: Governance
tour.description: Review the GWC policies and runbooks that govern delivery control, approval boundaries, and notification behavior for the workspace itself.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines
tour.description: Walk through the GitHub Actions workflows that validate the workspace, publish Powers, and perform BMAD-specific release validation with overlay and E2E tests.

tour.title: Tests
tour.description: Examine the Python unit tests and shell scripts that validate power distribution contracts, runtime installers, multi-host setup, and workspace commands.
